Chicory is a perennial that forms long, stick-like stems 
and ragged, widely spaced bunches of leaves, 
sometimes in tight heads or in loose formations.
The outer leaves may be green, white, or 
red, depending on variety, and have a 
strong, slightly bitter taste.  The inner 
leaves are usually paler in color and 
milder in flavor.
